# Endpoint-preserving numerical representation of the complete filter

2026-10-29 HST, E003/S169. Ordinary argument and contract BEFORE execution.
Previous turn: PROGRESS, 1fb110e enclosed the complete coupled analytic
filter residual. Preserve that result, P32, the closed audit and all
original physical norms. The full stable-wormhole objective is incomplete.

The selected certificate is ||y_num-yhat||Et<=1.70e31 for the SAME
actual-domain filter. This is an error allowance, not a known error or
a free physical margin. Parameter rounding, profile quadrature and its
coefficient errors must ALL enter. No finite matter-mode calculation or
change to the quantum action is used.

## Numerical object and the domain implication

Keep H=-partial_x((2x+a x^2)partial_x), x=(L-z)/gamma and the exact
finite-Q reconstruction T of 1b04eae. The input norm for this calculation is

    X(f)=sqrt(gamma)||(1+H)^(9/4) f||L2(dx),

and the output is the ORIGINAL Et norm, et=ell_t/N. H is an auxiliary
profile generator, not a replacement matter operator or physical norm.
The actual paired mass/log realization, complementary adjoint, composed
squares, fixed clock/period/spin/scale and regular bolt remain. T retains
J(0)=0, (Q^2 J'/z^4)(L)=0 and its COMPLETE Volterra return.

The numerical object is a finite resolvent-product expansion with EXACT
rational stored coefficients and conjugate pairs. It is a representation
of a function, not point samples or an interpolant. Its evaluator returns
outward intervals for that represented function. Choosing midpoint point
values and fitting another interpolant would be a different, uncertified
caller and is outside this certificate.

Use B(p)=(p+1/4)(p+1/2)(p+1)(p+3). Each numerical summand has the form
B(H)^-1(H+mu)^-1 delta_b; a constant term uses B(H)^-1 delta_b. All
Re(mu)>0. Thus EVERY summand has the required ultraviolet p^-4 decay
before coefficient rounding. The first three bolt-log moments cancel
algebraically within each product. The additional r=(H+muY)^-1 f used
by T is retained. The complete paired-domain reconstruction therefore
has the same form-domain realization as the analytic trial. Independent
rounding of partial-fraction Q coefficients is expressly not the object.

The full source/energy comparison below proves a finite quantitative
map X->Et. The outer logarithm requires special care: an L2 source cannot
be multiplied by log(z) using its supremum. Factor the vanishing powers
in the ORIGINAL canonical strong rows before taking norms instead.

## A complete quantitative X-to-Et comparison

Use the exact rows(p,c,bs,x) generator of 1b04eae. Its eight basis entries
are r,h_r,f,h_f,Hf,h_Hf,H^2 f,W, with h_f=q2 f_x and
W(z)=int_0^z (t Q''-4Q')'r dt. For X(f)=1,

    ||r||,||f||,||Hf||,||H^2 f|| <=1,
    ||h_r||,||h_f||,||h_Hf|| <=sqrt(Q2(L))/gamma,
    ||W|| <=L Dmax.

These follow from the complete spectral calculus, muY>1, p^j<=
(1+p)^(9/4), j<=2, and ||sqrt(Q2)partial_s H^j f||<=1, j<=1.
They retain dz=gamma dx. The W bound follows from its full Volterra
integral, with Dmax already certified for the actual polynomial Q.

On 0<=s<=L-.01, enclose each coefficient over the same whole cells as
1b04eae and take its GLOBAL maximum. Do not sum a global input norm
once per cell. Add the reference classical canonical rows fn,fu explicitly
(these are subtracted by the reused generator); their norm constants are
L^2 sum |c_name,j|, since the three profiles r,f,Hf have norm <=1.
The test bounds CU,CV are for the original Uxi,Vxi and include their
global York realization. No model adjoint replaces it.

On 0<z<=.01 the weighted strong-row coefficients are A(z)+B(z)log(z).
BOTH A and B are analytic on |z|<=.02 and divisible by z^2. Here is
the power count in the original action, not a smooth reflected extension.
The reconstruction coefficients start at z^4 (or z^5); up to four
derivatives can remove at most four powers. Background M0,N0,A0 have
at most z^-2, their squares at most z^-4, and every such product pairs
with the corresponding undifferentiated or twice differentiated field.
The terms div_phi(w), div_nu(A0), Delta(w) and Delta(nu/z^2) have at
worst order z^0 before the original z^2 row weight. Differentiating
log(z) introduces exactly the corresponding derivative powers, never
an extra negative order. Hf and h_f are kept as separate basis elements;
the same power count holds coefficient by coefficient. Q2 has no zero
in this outer disk. This establishes the removable zero, including the
coefficient of H^2 f for which a pointwise trace was not supplied.

If M_A,M_B enclose the complete |z|=.02 circle, maximum modulus applied
to A/z^2,B/z^2 gives on the whole outer interval b=.01

    |A+B log z| <=(b/.02)^2 [M_A+|log b| M_B].

There is therefore no unproved endpoint trace or log multiplier. Include
all 64 interval arcs, as in the accepted outer-row proof. Combining the
global coefficient maxima with the eight input bounds gives the entire
local/reference dual constant C_local, through CU and CV.

The accepted interpolation theorem supplies the COMPLETE nonlocal
geodesic dual coefficient Kgeo*Cflow times X. For the actual-minus-
reference response use the existing uniform reconstruction derivative
constants S0,S1,S2 and Dconn0:

 U0=S0 X, U1=sqrt(10) S1 X, U2=10(S2+Dconn0 S1)X.

Charge the entire cap with its known 1e18 coefficient; no localization is
assumed for a numerical error. Retain the gain-two kernel, finite second
contact, annulus, row-subtracted global return, constant-contact global
return and curvature polynomial. All exact UV logarithms, common
regulators, angular/thermal sums and finite-domain returns are those of
2d8ef11. The final vacuum/energy comparison costs cE ||Tf||Et. Positivity
and the actual form identity give

    ||Tf||Et <= C_E X(f),
    C_E=(C_local+Kgeo*Cflow+C_quantum)/(1-cE).           (1)

Verify cE<1. This is a fixed-seed computational output comparison, not
the original C5 physical admission or a nonlinear-neighborhood theorem.

## Correlated parameter error, before numerical pole quadrature

Write the accepted f2/At as N(p)/D(p), with degree(N)=2, degree(D)=6:

 N=K0*kappa*(Cv+delta p)*(p+Cv lambda_n),
 D=(p+muT)(p+muS)(p+lambda_l)
                 *(p^2+d1 p+d0)*(p+lambda_n).

Round primitive profile parameters and At to explicitly stored rational
centers. The physical geometry and H,T are NOT rounded or replaced.
The difference from the correlated exact parameters is charged using
the polynomial numerator

    C(p)=(At/At_num)N(p)D_num(p)-N_num(p)D(p).

Perform this cancellation COEFFICIENT BY COEFFICIENT before intervals
in p. The complete parameter difference is At_num*C/(D D_num).
Under p=t/(1-t), it is At_num*(1-t)^4 C_t/(D_t D_num,t).
The whole-spectral density <=1/2 gives

 X_parameter^2 <= At_num^2 gamma/2
    *int_0^1 (1-t)^(3/2)|C_t/(D_t D_num,t)|^2 dt.       (2)

Enclose every whole t cell, including the infinite endpoint. Use positive
polynomial denominator coefficients and their Bernstein lower guard.
This charges original parameter uncertainty as well as the selected
rational rounding. It does not independently round nodal coefficients
over the full parameter box, losing the common rational cancellation.

## Finite contour expansion and every quadrature/rounding error

Let G(p)=B(p)N_num(p)/D_num(p), g_inf its constant at infinity.
Keep the large-mass pole lambda_n,num as an EXACT rational residue Rn.
Group all other poles in circles (center,radius)
(2,1/4),(4/3,1/5),(2/3,1/10). The first contains muT and lambda_l,
the second both quadratic roots, and the third muS. Verify inclusion,
disjointness and a pole-free annulus from radius r/2 to 3r/2.

For Ntheta=256 equally spaced, half-shifted nodes on each circle,

    mu_j=center+r exp(2pi i(j+1/2)/Ntheta),
    w_j=-(mu_j-center)G(-mu_j)/Ntheta,
    f_num(p)=At_num/B(p) [g_inf+Rn/(p+lambda_n,num)
                                  +sum_j w_j/(p+mu_j)].         (3)

The sign follows from the residue of G(-mu). Store EXACT rational centers
for the complex nodes and weights, paired by conjugation. Preserve the
product B in (3); do not replace it by independently rounded residues.
For Re(mu)>=m>0, m<=1, the complete spectral comparison gives

 ||(1+H)^(9/4)B(H)^-1(H+mu)^-1 delta_b|| <=256/(3m),

since B(p)>=(1+p)^4/256. For a constant B^-1 term the bound is
256/sqrt(5). The corresponding squared-resolvent norm is <=256/(sqrt(13)m^2).
Thus weight and node rounding have explicit costs, respectively
256*|dw|/(3m) and 256*|w|*|dmu|/(sqrt(13)m^2).
Include g_inf and Rn rounding if they are not stored exactly.

The operator-valued integrand is analytic in each specified annulus:
the profile poles lie strictly inside the inner circle and Re(mu)>0
keeps the auxiliary resolvent away from its spectrum. Its Fourier/Laurent
series is absolutely convergent in the X norm. Summing the aliased
coefficients of the trapezoidal rule gives

    X_quad <=At_num sqrt(gamma) sum_circles
      [M_outer/((3/2)^Ntheta-1)+M_inner/(2^Ntheta-1)],   (4)

where M_R=R sup_|mu-c|=R |G(-mu)|*256/(3m_R).
Bound G by its exact polynomial numerator and the positive distances to
all denominator poles. For the quadratic use
|D2(-mu)|>=distance(mu,d1/2)^2-|d0-d1^2/4|.
No separation of nearly coincident roots is used. Equation (4) includes
the COMPLETE spectral error, not selected input frequencies.

Test C_E*(X_parameter+X_quad+X_round)<=1.70e31. If excessive, identify
the dominant entry and its required reduction. Do not replace C_E by
the allowed ceiling or claim a larger error invalidates the construction.

## Executable point/endpoint interface and the actual return

Evaluate each product through its exact partial-fraction identity,
recomputing the residues from the stored product poles with outward
arithmetic. The coefficients are never independently stored/rounded.
Use standard Q_nu(w), w>1, with nu(nu+1)=mu/a. Its normalization follows
[DLMF 14.3.7 and 14.3.10](https://dlmf.nist.gov/14.3), with the type-3
branch in [python-flint's documented Legendre evaluator](https://python-flint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/acb.html#flint.acb.legendre_q).
Check Q0(w)=log((w+1)/(w-1))/2 and Q1=w Q0-1 before using the interface.
The pinned local runtime, not a new library version, remains authoritative.

Keep the common bolt logarithm analytically. A product with at least four
poles has sum residue*mu^j=0 for j=0,1,2. Its bolt value is therefore
-sum residue*digamma(nu+1), without subtracting divergent Q values.
The bolt flux vanishes. The endpoint limiting formula is used, not a
sample taken at a small artificial radius.

The Volterra coefficient (z Q''-4Q')' is a polynomial of degree <=4.
Expand it in P_j(w). For nonresonant nu,

 int P_j(w)Q_nu(w) dw
   =(w^2-1)(P_j Q_nu'-P_j' Q_nu)
                          /[nu(nu+1)-j(j+1)].         (5)

This follows directly from the two Legendre equations. At w=1 the
primitive equals -1/[nu(nu+1)-j(j+1)]. Use (5) between the ORIGINAL
outer endpoint and the evaluation point, with dz=-gamma dw/a. This
encloses the entire finite-domain return, including the bolt limit;
there is no truncated tail or invented homogeneous solution. The exact
T formula then returns xi,nu,u,J and W with rounding enclosures.

The representation error is already the GLOBAL Et bound from (1)-(4).
Point evaluations demonstrate and test the implemented interface; they
do not replace that bound. Their returned intervals enclose the SAME
finite-product function, so no additional sampled-field error is silently
declared zero. Any later scalar integration or application using this
interface must propagate its actual evaluation intervals.

Remaining to-do list: this numerical caller certificate, last filter and
full signed G_t/Z_r; every original coupled/source/graph/physical/boundary/
mass budget; nonlinear admission/contraction/existence, compatibility,
physical matching, semiclassical validity/noise and all-sector stability;
the full stable semiclassical wormhole objective.

from pathlib import Path

import current_coupled_first_filter_test as old
arb,ctx,dec,enc,J=old.arb,old.ctx,old.dec,old.enc,old.J
from flint import acb

 'operators/paired_filter_profile.py','evidence/current-coupled-first-filter-test-attempt2.json',
 'evidence/current-coupled-first-filter-test-attempt2-verification.json',*old.INPUTS]))

def qball(q):return arb(q.numerator)/arb(q.denominator)
def qenc(q):return dict(numerator=str(q.numerator),denominator=str(q.denominator))
def middle(v):
 m,_,e=v.mid_rad_10exp(110);return Fraction(int(m))*Fraction(10)**int(e)
def cmiddle(v):return middle(v.real),middle(v.imag)
def cball(v):return acb(qball(v[0]),qball(v[1]))
def cenc(v):return dict(real=qenc(v[0]),imag=qenc(v[1]))
def polyadd(*vs):
 out=[0]*max(map(len,vs))
 for v in vs:
  for j,a in enumerate(v):out[j]+=a
 return out
def polymul(v,w):
 out=[0]*(len(v)+len(w)-1)
 for j,a in enumerate(v):
  for k,b in enumerate(w):out[j+k]+=a*b
 return out
def polyeval(v,x):
 out=0
 for a in reversed(v):out=out*x+a
 return out
def polypoles(poles):
 out=[1]
 for pole in poles:out=polymul(out,[pole,1])
 return out

def output_comparison(p,c,bs):
 L,a,ga=p['L'],p['a'],p['gamma'];lr.model_rows(p,c)
 base=lr.result('current-coupled-first-filter-test-attempt2')['local_return']
 maxima=[[arb(0)]*8 for _ in range(4)];rows=[]

  rows.append([[enc(up(v)) for v in row] for row in rr])
  if i%40==0:print(json.dumps(dict(uniform_row_cells=i,total=len(base['cells']))),flush=True)
 outerA=[[arb(0)]*8 for _ in range(4)];outerB=[[arb(0)]*8 for _ in range(4)]
 for i in range(64):
  theta=arb((2*i+1)*arb.pi()/64,arb.pi()/64)
  z=acb(theta.cos(),theta.sin())*arb('.02')
  x=J([(L-z)/ga,acb(1)]+[acb(0)]*8)
  r0=lr.rows(p,c,bs,x,acb(0));r1=lr.rows(p,c,bs,x,acb(1))
  for h in range(4):
   for j in range(8):
    outerA[h][j]=lr.maximum(outerA[h][j],abs(r0[h][j]))
    outerB[h][j]=lr.maximum(outerB[h][j],abs(r1[h][j]-r0[h][j]))
 b=arb('.01');outer=[]
 for h in range(4):
  row=[]

   v=(b/arb('.02'))**2*(outerA[h][j]+abs(b.log())*outerB[h][j])
   maxima[h][j]=lr.maximum(maxima[h][j],v);row.append(enc(v))
  outer.append(row)
 Dmax=cs('current-source-adapted-local-return-attempt4')['Dmax']
 flux=(2*ga*L+a*L*L).sqrt()/ga
 bb=[arb(1),flux,arb(1),flux,arb(1),flux,arb(1),L*Dmax]
 norms=[sum((v*w for v,w in zip(row,bb)),arb(0)) for row in maxima]
 for j,name in enumerate(['fn','fu']):
  norms[j]+=L**2*sum((up(c[name+'_'+k]) for k in ['r','f','g']),arb(0))
 CU,CV=[dec(base['constants'][k]) for k in ['CU','CV']]
 local=CU*(norms[0]+norms[2])+CV*(norms[1]+norms[3])
 shape=lr.result('current-source-adapted-fractional-return');fc=cs('current-source-adapted-fractional-return')
 S=[dec(v) for v in shape['derivative_accounting']['reconstructed_reference_derivative_constants']]
 D0=dec(shape['connection_tensor_derivative_bounds'][0])
 U0=S[0];U1=arb(10).sqrt()*S[1];U2=10*(S[2]+D0*S[1])
 oc=cs('current-source-adapted-complete-response-test');C,B2,beta=p['C'],p['B2'],p['beta']
 CG,CD=oc['test_gradient_constant'],oc['test_Laplacian_constant']
 factor=2/(B2*beta);qang=arb(2000)**4;pi=arb.pi();K=arb('1e10');sp=arb('1e-24')
 br=(sp/(4*K)).sqrt();bg=K*(arb(1)/4+2*((arb(1)/400)/br).log())
 qparts=dict(local_gain_two=factor*2*pi*C*(sp*U2**2/3+bg*U1**2).sqrt()*(sp*(3*CD**2/8+CG**2/4)/3+bg*CG**2).sqrt(),
  full_annulus=factor*2*pi*arb('4e8')*C*(arb(400)/128).log()*U1*CG,
  finite_second_contact=factor*arb('1e13')*C*U1*CG,
  global_row_return=factor*oc['complete_global_gluing_coefficient']*C*U0*CV,
  complete_cap_contact=factor*arb('1e18')*qang**2/C*(1+1/arb(5).sqrt())*U0*CV,
  constant_contact_return=factor*oc['constant_contact_gluing_coefficient']*C*U0*CV,
  curvature_polynomial=factor*100*C*(U1*CG/(36*pi)+816*U0*CV/(960*pi)))
 eps=cs('current-complete-polynomial-weak-transfer')['epsilon']
 ce=arb('1e-21')/((1-eps)*arb('.99')*(1-arb('1.179e-8')))+eps/(1-eps)
 assert ce<1
 geo=c['actual_reference_fractional_output_coefficient']*fc['actual_reconstruction_fractional_comparison']
 CE=up((local+geo+sum(qparts.values(),arb(0)))/(1-ce))
 return CE,dict(constants={k:enc(v) for k,v in dict(complete_local_dual=local,

def profile_parameters(p,c):
 actual={k:c[k] for k in ['K0','kappa','Cv','delta','muT','muS','d1','d0']}
 actual.update(lambda_l=p['a']*p['ell']*(p['ell']+1),lambda_n=c['large_mass_lambda'],At=p['At'])
 nominal={k:middle(v) for k,v in actual.items()}
 def polys(v):
  N=polymul([v['Cv'],v['delta']],[v['Cv']*v['lambda_n'],1])
  N=[v['K0']*v['kappa']*x for x in N]
  D=polymul(polypoles([v[k] for k in ['muT','muS','lambda_l','lambda_n']]),[v['d0'],v['d1'],1])
  return N,D
 return actual,nominal,polys(actual),polys(nominal)

def parameter_error(p,actual,nominal,ad,nd):
 Na,Da=ad;Nn,Dn=nd;amplitude=qball(nominal['At'])
 ratio=actual['At']/amplitude
 diff=polyadd([ratio*v for v in polymul(Na,[qball(v) for v in Dn])],
              [-v for v in polymul([qball(v) for v in Nn],Da)])
 assert len(diff)==9
 gard=lambda d:min((arb(v).lower()/comb(6,j) for j,v in enumerate(d)))
 Dnb=[qball(v) for v in Dn];ga=arb(gard(Da));gn=arb(gard(Dnb));assert ga>0 and gn>0
 total=arb(0);cells=[];count=1024
 for i in range(count):
  tl=arb(i)/count;tu=arb(i+1)/count;wl=1-tu;wu=1-tl
  # Exact integration endpoints are rational; use outward positive guards.
  tl=arb(max(arb(0),tl.lower()));wl=arb(max(arb(0),wl.lower()))
  tu=up(tu);wu=up(wu)
  dl=sum((arb(v.lower())*tl**j*wl**(6-j) for j,v in enumerate(Da)),arb(0))
  nl=sum((arb(v.lower())*tl**j*wl**(6-j) for j,v in enumerate(Dnb)),arb(0))
  dl=arb(max(ga.lower(),dl.lower()));nl=arb(max(gn.lower(),nl.lower()))
  num=sum((up(v)*tu**j*wu**(8-j) for j,v in enumerate(diff)),arb(0))
  cost=up(wu**arb('1.5')*(num/(dl*nl))**2/count)
  total+=cost;cells.append(enc(cost))
 X=up(amplitude*(p['gamma']*total/2).sqrt())
 return X,dict(cross_numerator=[enc(v) for v in diff],whole_spectral_cells=cells,
  denominator_Bernstein_guards=[enc(ga),enc(gn)],parameter_X_error=enc(X))

def contour_representation(p,nominal,nd,count=256):
 Nn,Dn=nd;B=[Fraction(1,4),Fraction(1,2),Fraction(1),Fraction(3)]
 Bpoly=polypoles(B);Gnum=polymul(Bpoly,Nn);ginf=Gnum[-1]
 ln=nominal['lambda_n'];other=polymul(polypoles([nominal[k] for k in ['muT','muS','lambda_l']]),[nominal['d0'],nominal['d1'],1])
 Rn=polyeval(Gnum,-ln)/polyeval(other,-ln)
 field=dict(amplitude=qenc(nominal['At']),base_poles=[qenc(v) for v in B],
  constant=qenc(ginf),large_pole=qenc(ln),large_pole_residue=qenc(Rn),upper_half_nodes=[])
 Gn=[qball(v) for v in Gnum];Dnball=[qball(v) for v in Dn]
 circles=[(Fraction(2),Fraction(1,4)),(Fraction(4,3),Fraction(1,5)),(Fraction(2,3),Fraction(1,10))]
 qcost=rcost=arb(0);details=[]
 h=qball(nominal['d1'])/2;e=qball(nominal['d0'])-h*h

  C,R=qball(center),qball(radius)

  for key in ['muT','muS','lambda_l','lambda_n']:
   dist=abs(qball(nominal[key])-C)

  assert dh+abs(e).sqrt()<R/2 or dh-abs(e).sqrt()>3*R/2
  bounds=[]
  for rr in [R/2,3*R/2]:
   mindeg=old.minimum(arb(1),C-rr);assert mindeg>0
   den=arb(1)
   for key in ['muT','muS','lambda_l','lambda_n']:
    dist=abs(qball(nominal[key])-C);gap=rr-dist if dist<rr else dist-rr
    assert gap>0;den*=gap
   gap=rr-dh if dh<rr else dh-rr
   dg=gap*gap-abs(e);assert dg>0;den*=dg
   numerator=sum((up(v)*(C+rr)**j for j,v in enumerate(Gn)),arb(0))
   bounds.append(up(rr*numerator/den*256/(3*mindeg)))
  quad=bounds[1]/((arb(3)/2)**count-1)+bounds[0]/(arb(2)**count-1)
  qcost+=quad;round_circle=arb(0)
  for j in range(count//2):
   theta=2*arb.pi()*(arb(j)+arb('.5'))/count
   pole=acb(C)+R*acb(theta.cos(),theta.sin())
   weight=-(pole-C)*polyeval(Gn,-pole)/polyeval(Dnball,-pole)/count
   pn,wn=cmiddle(pole),cmiddle(weight);pb,wb=cball(pn),cball(wn)
   dmu=up(abs(pole-pb));dw=up(abs(weight-wb))
   mm=arb(min(arb(1).lower(),pole.real.lower(),pb.real.lower()));assert mm>0
   term=256*dw/(3*mm)+256*up(abs(wb))*dmu/(arb(13).sqrt()*mm**2)

   annular_norm_bounds=[enc(v) for v in bounds],quadrature_X_before_scale=enc(quad),rounding_X_before_scale=enc(round_circle)))
 scale=qball(nominal['At'])*p['gamma'].sqrt()
 return field,up(scale*qcost),up(scale*rcost),details

def execute():

"""Finite resolvent-product field; exact stored fractions, outward queries.

The product representation, not independently rounded partial fractions,
defines the field. T uses the original finite geometry and entire return.
"""
from fractions import Fraction
from math import comb
from flint import arb,acb

def real(q):
    return arb(int(q['numerator']))/arb(int(q['denominator']))

def complex_ball(q):
    return acb(real(q['real']),real(q['imag']))

def polyval(c,x):
    out=x*0
    for a in reversed(c):out=out*x+a
    return out

def polynomials():
    P=[[arb(1)],[arb(0),arb(1)]]
    for j in range(1,4):
        row=[arb(0)]*(j+2)
        for k,v in enumerate(P[j]):row[k+1]+=(2*j+1)*v/(j+1)
        for k,v in enumerate(P[j-1]):row[k]-=j*v/(j+1)
        P.append(row)
    return P

class PairedFilterProfile:
    def __init__(self,parameters,bolt_coefficients,field):
        self.p=parameters;self.bs=bolt_coefficients;self.data=field
        self.a=parameters['a'];self.ga=parameters['gamma'];self.L=parameters['L']
        self.muY=4*self.a/3;self.amplitude=real(field['amplitude'])
        self.base=[acb(real(v)) for v in field['base_poles']]
        terms=[(acb(real(field['constant'])),[]),
               (acb(real(field['large_pole_residue'])),[acb(real(field['large_pole']))])]
        for node in field['upper_half_nodes']:
            pole=complex_ball(node['pole']);weight=complex_ball(node['weight'])
            terms.extend([(weight,[pole]),(weight.conjugate(),[pole.conjugate()])])
        # Aggregate common residues in RAM, always derived from the PRODUCTS.
        common=self.base+[acb(self.muY)]
        weights=[acb(0)]*len(common);individual=[]
        for weight,extra in terms:
            poles=common+extra
            for j,mu in enumerate(poles):
                den=acb(1)
                for k,other in enumerate(poles):
                    if k!=j:den*=other-mu
                assert not den.contains(0)
                coefficient=weight/den
                if j<len(common):weights[j]+=coefficient
                else:individual.append((mu,coefficient))
        self.partials=list(zip(common,weights))+individual
        self.P=polynomials()
        # Original (z Q''-4 Q')' in Legendre polynomial coordinates.
        # Q(z) is reconstructed from its exact bolt expansion.
        Q=[arb(0)]*7
        for j,b in enumerate(bolt_coefficients):
            for k in range(j+1):Q[k]+=b*comb(j,k)*self.L**(j-k)*(-1)**k
        Dz=[(j+2)*(j+1)*(j-3)*Q[j+2] for j in range(5)]
        g=self.ga/self.a;z0=self.L+g;power=[arb(0)]*5
        for j,b in enumerate(Dz):
            for k in range(j+1):power[k]+=b*comb(j,k)*z0**(j-k)*(-g)**k
        leg=[arb(0)]*5
        for j in range(4,-1,-1):
            leg[j]=power[j]/self.P[j][-1]
            for k,b in enumerate(self.P[j]):power[k]-=leg[j]*b
        assert all(v.contains(0) for v in power)
        self.Dleg=leg;self.outer_w=1+self.a*self.L/self.ga
        self.outer_primitive=None

    def kernel(self,mu,w,bolt=False):
        degree=((1+4*mu/self.a).sqrt()-1)/2
        if bolt:
            return -(degree+1).digamma(),acb(0),degree
        q=acb(w).legendre_q(degree,0,type=3)
        qplus=acb(w).legendre_q(degree+1,0,type=3)
        flux=(degree+1)*(qplus-w*q)
        assert q.is_finite() and flux.is_finite()
        return q,flux,degree

    def primitive(self,mu,q,flux,w,bolt=False):
        total=acb(0)
        for j,(dj,Pj) in enumerate(zip(self.Dleg,self.P)):
            den=mu/self.a-j*(j+1);assert not den.contains(0)
            if bolt:numerator=acb(-1)
            else:
                dp=[k*Pj[k] for k in range(1,len(Pj))]
                numerator=polyval(Pj,w)*flux-(w*w-1)*polyval(dp,w)*q
            total+=dj*numerator/den
        return total

    def prepare_return(self):
        if self.outer_primitive is not None:return
        total=acb(0)
        for mu,coefficient in self.partials:
            q,flux,_=self.kernel(mu,self.outer_w)
            total+=coefficient*self.primitive(mu,q,flux,self.outer_w)
        self.outer_primitive=total

    def at_outer(self):
        return {k:arb(0) for k in ['xi','nu','u','J','W']}

    def at(self,s,bolt=False):
        if bolt:s=arb(0)
        else:assert s>0 and s<self.L
        self.prepare_return();w=1+self.a*s/self.ga
        rv=fv=hr=pv=acb(0)
        for mu,coefficient in self.partials:
            q,flux,_=self.kernel(mu,w,bolt=bolt)
            rv+=coefficient*q;fv+=(self.muY-mu)*coefficient*q
            hr+=coefficient*flux
            pv+=coefficient*self.primitive(mu,q,flux,w,bolt=bolt)
        W=self.ga/self.a*(self.outer_primitive-pv)
        vals=[]
        for v in [rv,fv,hr,W]:
            assert v.is_finite() and v.imag.contains(0)
            vals.append(v.real*self.amplitude)
        rv,fv,hr,W=vals;x=s/self.ga;z=self.L-s
        # Geometry is evaluated by the same exact finite-Q jets as the proof.
        from current_source_adapted_fractional_return import J,geometry_jets
        xx=J([x,arb(1)]+[arb(0)]*4)
        zz,q2,R,q=geometry_jets(self.p,self.bs,xx)
        RR=R.c[0];Rx=R.d().c[0];M=z*q.d().d().c[0]+4*self.ga*q.d().c[0]
        nu=z**4/(3*self.L**5)*(-z*RR*fv+(z*RR*self.muY-M)*rv-(7*self.ga*RR-z*Rx)*hr+W)
        u=z**4/self.L**5*(z*RR*fv+(2*M/3-z*RR*self.muY)*rv+(5*self.ga*RR-z*Rx)*hr-2*W/3)
        xi=2*nu+4*self.ga*z**4*RR*hr/(3*self.L**5)
        rx=(self.muY*rv-fv)/2 if bolt else hr/q2.c[0]
        Jvalue=-2*z**5*rx/(3*self.ga*self.L**5)
        return dict(xi=xi,nu=nu,u=u,J=Jvalue,W=W,f=fv,r=rv,hr=hr)
